notes.text: For ראש in the Edumean ostraca see discussion s.v. rwš n. As with other words frequent in compounds, we have assigned independent entries only where the sum of the compound is more than the sum of its parts. Traditionally in Jewish Lexicography, "head" and "poison" are treated as two different words (i.e. רֹאשׁ in BH as well). This is now considered to be unlikely. The connection is presumably the source of a snake's venom.

notes.text: This verb, unique to Targum Proverbs, where it always renders the unusual usage of Hebrew פרע in the sense of "to avoid" or "to remove" or the like, is of totally uncertain origin. Even the correct root form is uncertain. It could be ršš, rwš, or even a derivative of rʕš in a late Babylonian or Palestinian dialect. The Peshitta rendering differs in each case, so it offers no guidance. Nor do any of the possible roots bear any obvious relationship to the normal usages of BH פרע. We suspect in the final analysis that it is an invention of the translator based on the common BH word רָשׁ, "poor person", which is also found used only in this Aramaic text, but the motivation for such a rendering must remain obscure.

notes.text: We take this unusual usage to be a metathesized form of šry conflated with ršy#2. The semantics have been developed due to three BH usages with conflated pronunciation in Samaritan Hebrew, i.e. הוֹאִיל with its two meanings "to allow (?)" and "to begin" along with החל "to begin". Note that this meaning is found only in the J targum of the Torah where such manipulation of forms and meanings based on Hebrew word play is common. Contrariwise, however, the noun רשו "priorness" (see s.v. ryšw) is found only in the late A text. All is very dubious.

formsNote: In Syriac the plural form varies with the meaning (perhaps other than in poetry): "chief, noble one," etc. follows the adjectival, reduplicative patterns with or without final -ān (see s.v. rb adj.), while "teacher" uses ܪ̈ܲܒܿܵܢܸܐ; JBA pl.רבי٠ רבוותא; many compounds keep the singular form rb even in the plural of the compound, e.g. ܪܒܥܠܢ̈ܐ "chief shepherd"; JLA, LJLA use both רברבין and רברבנין as the plural for "noble". In Gal. forms with doubled /b/ display a vowel shift /a/>/e/, hence rebbī "rabbi", etc. Compare rbwn. The multiplicity of plural forms in Mandaic currently defies analysis!
